symptom: A synthetic Linux nested directory open with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW followed an intermediate symlink and returned an FD for a decoy vault. Walking the same alias as a separate dirfd-relative no-follow component rejected it; walking ordinary real components succeeded. No publication or production failure was observed.
lesson: O_NOFOLLOW applies to the final component of each open call, not to all intermediate path components. An attacker-controlled ancestor symlink can redirect a nested directory FD despite O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW. An explicitly trusted root FD and per-component no-follow walk reject this specific alias while admitting normal directories.
guardrail: Do not treat O_NOFOLLOW on a nested absolute path as full-path directory authentication. For a future Linux research candidate, start from an explicitly trusted root and review per-component openat or openat2 resolution constraints, then separately test concurrent ancestor renames, mounts, canonical-path reachability, same-FD read/write namespace, collision handling and crash durability. Never infer production authority, weaken strict readback, or delete files by stale pathname.
